hypothesis: A cart with OVS-PIECE x6 and OVS-TWOPACK x3 needs 12 WIDGET units but only 10 are stocked. Each line is validated against available stock alone (6<=10, 6<=10) and entries sharing the inventory item are not summed in ensureInventoryLevels, so the order completes and reserves 12 > 10, failing no_oversell.

The default in-memory locking provider only serializes within a process. Two carts each needing 6 of 10 WIDGET completed at once on different servers can both pass the availability check and both reserve, giving 12 reserved > 10 stocked.
Completing the same cart twice concurrently on two servers: the cart lock is process-local, so both pass the 'already completed' check and both create orders or return different order ids.

createReservationItems_ writes reserved_quantity = stale level.reserved_quantity + adjustment. With stock ample, many carts completing concurrently across two servers (no shared lock) read the same counter and overwrite each other, so reserved_quantity ends below the sum of reservations.

Same cart completed 5 times concurrently on one server. The cart lock should serialize them and later calls should return the existing order; if the completed check races, multiple orders get created or different order ids returned.
Stock is lowered after the cart is built; completing should fail inventory validation. If stock is read at one location and reserved at another, the order succeeds anyway and oversells.
Single cart with PIECE x10 and TWOPACK x5 (20 units) vs 10 stock, plus a SOLO case; each line alone fits in the check but the sum exceeds stock.
